transcript: Apple Inc. Q3 2025 earnings call. Revenue reached $94.9 billion, up 5% year-over-year. Net income was $21.4 billion. Gross margin stood at 46.2%, driven by favorable mix. iPhone revenue was $45.7 billion, representing stable demand. iPad grew 23% to $7.2 billion. Services reached an all-time record of $24.2 billion, up 14%. Tim Cook highlighted the rollout of Apple Intelligence, the personal intelligence system built into macOS, iOS, and iPadOS, noting that customers and developers are seeing immediate productivity boosts from integrated writing tools and on-device private cloud compute features.

Microsoft Corp. Q4 2025 earnings call. Revenue reached $64.7 billion, an increase of 15% year-over-year. Operating income grew 15% to $27.9 billion. Microsoft Cloud revenue was $36.8 billion, up 19%, driven by Azure and other cloud services. Satya Nadella commented that Azure AI now has over 60,000 active customers, growing 60% year-over-year, with rising average spend. Capital expenditures were $13.9 billion to support cloud infrastructure and AI capacity. Nadella emphasized the continuous scale of Copilot integration across Microsoft 365, Github Enterprise, and cloud developer platforms.

Alphabet Inc. Q2 2025 earnings call. Consolidated revenues were $84.7 billion, up 14% year-over-year, or 15% in constant currency. Google Search & Other revenue was $48.5 billion, up 14%. YouTube ads grew 13% to $8.7 billion. Google Cloud revenues surged 28% to $10.3 billion, with operating income reaching $1.1 billion. Sundar Pichai discussed the widespread rollout of AI Overviews in Google Search and highlighted the cost efficiencies gained from custom TPU infrastructure. Pichai detailed how Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash models are helping developers build production-grade AI agents, significantly reducing inference costs while maintaining high-quality outputs.

Amazon.com, Inc. Q2 2025 earnings call. Net sales increased 10% to $148.0 billion. AWS segment sales increased 19% year-over-year to $26.3 billion, with an annualized revenue run rate exceeding $105 billion. AWS operating income was $8.9 billion. Andy Jassy highlighted the rapid adoption of Amazon Bedrock and AWS Trainium/Inferentia chips for custom model training. Jassy noted that Amazon is seeing substantial interest in generative AI applications across corporate clients, with customer spending stabilizing and migrating toward modernized cloud databases. E-commerce margins also expanded due to regionalization of fulfillment centers.

NVIDIA Corp. Q1 2026 earnings call. Record quarterly revenue of $26.0 billion, up 18% from the previous quarter and up 262% from a year ago. Data Center revenue was $22.6 billion, up 427% year-over-year, driven by demand for the Hopper GPU platform (H100) and initial shipments of Blackwell architectures. Co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang remarked that the next industrial revolution has begun. Enterprises and nations are partnering with NVIDIA to shift trillion-dollar traditional data centers to accelerated computing and build a new type of data center, AI factories, to produce a new commodity: artificial intelligence.

Tesla, Inc. Q2 2025 earnings call. Total revenues were $25.5 billion, up 2% year-over-year despite a challenging delivery environment. Automotive revenues were $20.0 billion. Energy generation and storage revenue reached a record $3.0 billion, up 100% year-over-year. Elon Musk discussed ongoing progress in Full Self-Driving (FSD) Version 12.5, which runs on their proprietary AI Hardware 4.0. Musk also highlighted that Tesla is expanding its Dojo supercomputer cluster to accelerate autonomous neural network training and announced that limited production of Optimus humanoid robots for internal use will begin in 2026.
